x="90" y="85" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="drnote" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=10;fillColor=#FFFBEB;strokeColor=#D97706;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>HA and DR: Multi-AZ plus in-region backups (no data leaves Thailand)</b><br><b>HA:</b> two AZs. RDS Multi-AZ fails over automatically. Stateless pods run in both AZs behind one ALB. One NAT gateway per AZ.<br><b>Backups in region:</b> RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery. AWS Backup snapshots of the ClickHouse and Redis disks. S3 versioning.<br><b>Not covered:</b> a full region outage. Recovery is a rebuild from the Kubernetes files; lost runs are sent again from GCP (a stored run never changes, and a resend is safe).<br><b>Weak point:</b> if the AZ that holds ClickHouse and Redis fails, Langfuse traces are unavailable until their disks are restored in the other AZ. Monitor grades are not affected.<br><b>To decide with the service owner:</b> recovery-time and data-loss targets, backup retention, who runs the restore drill." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="125" width="780" x="360" y="1130" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="asnote" parent="1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#232F3E;fontSize=10;fillColor=#FFFBEB;strokeColor=#D97706;spacing=8;rounded=1;arcSize=3;" value="<b>Assumptions and items to verify</b><br>1. Not verified for ap-southeast-7: WAF, Data Firehose, IAM Identity Center, Shield Advanced, AWS Backup, RDS PostgreSQL 17.<br>2. EKS is assumed; the plan says &quot;AWS Kubernetes cluster&quot;.<br>3. Shield Standard is automatic and free. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription.<br>4. Secrets Manager is new; the plan uses the Kubernetes secret store only.<br>5. No gateway endpoint exists for RDS. The cluster reaches RDS on a private IP. The interface endpoint is for the RDS management API; nothing in this stack calls it today.<br>6. Firehose pushes to Splunk and the SIEM; both need an HTTP endpoint that Firehose can reach.<br>7. The plan names no AWS image registry or deploy pipeline, so none is drawn. Each paid service needs a plan entry." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="125" width="750" x="1160" y="1130" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
HA and DR: Multi-AZ plus in-region backups (no data leaves Thailand)
HA: two AZs. RDS Multi-AZ fails over automatically. Stateless pods run in both AZs behind one ALB. One NAT gateway per AZ.
Backups in region: RDS automated backups with point-in-time recovery. AWS Backup snapshots of the ClickHouse and Redis disks. S3 versioning.
Not covered: a full region outage. Recovery is a rebuild from the Kubernetes files; lost runs are sent again from GCP (a stored run never changes, and a resend is safe).
Weak point: if the AZ that holds ClickHouse and Redis fails, Langfuse traces are unavailable until their disks are restored in the other AZ. Monitor grades are not affected.
To decide with the service owner: recovery-time and data-loss targets, backup retention, who runs the restore drill.

div.div:
Assumptions and items to verify
1. Not verified for ap-southeast-7: WAF, Data Firehose, IAM Identity Center, Shield Advanced, AWS Backup, RDS PostgreSQL 17.
2. EKS is assumed; the plan says "AWS Kubernetes cluster".
3. Shield Standard is automatic and free. Shield Advanced is a paid subscription.
4. Secrets Manager is new; the plan uses the Kubernetes secret store only.
5. No gateway endpoint exists for RDS. The cluster reaches RDS on a private IP. The interface endpoint is for the RDS management API; nothing in this stack calls it today.
6. Firehose pushes to Splunk and the SIEM; both need an HTTP endpoint that Firehose can reach.
7. The plan names no AWS image registry or deploy pipeline, so none is drawn. Each paid service needs a plan entry.
